title: Robert Ferringo Review 2026: Pricing, Record, Worth It?
description: Robert Ferringo review, checked 20 Nov 2026: Doc's Sports prices, the credit guarantee, his own posted logs recounted, and what buyers say.
dek: A longtime Doc's Sports writer and handicapper who sells picks in six sports through the Doc's store, from $25 a day to $850 a season. We recounted the pick logs Doc's links as proof of his runs: one confirms a winning football week, two come out lower than the advertised totals, and his hockey run won fewer than half its plays.

short_answer: Robert Ferringo is a real, named handicapper. Doc's Sports says he has written for it since 2004, and he still writes a weekly NFL column there in November 2026. He sells picks through the Doc's store, which publishes its prices, names its operator and gives a mailing address. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is not answered by anything we could open. His sales page is a wall of runs such as "100-57, +29,600" on 8 unit plays and "+65,080 NOV-DEC PROFIT", all chosen and graded by the seller. Doc's does link a few "documented" pick logs. We recounted three of them. A football week matched its claim exactly. A football week sold as "+6,070" adds up to +5,480 in the linked log, and an NHL run sold as "+9,935" totals +9,695 and won only 184 of 380 plays, with the profit coming from plus money prices and a few big plays.

Buyer evidence is thin and old. The one real forum fight about him, on Sportsbook Review in February 2014, pits a buyer who lost on a top rated total against a member who said he made money three straight years on the college basketball plays. Treat Ferringo as a high volume seller with partly checkable marketing, buy short, and log every play yourself.

guarantee: Ferringo's packages use the standard Doc's Sports guarantee. On weekly and monthly packages his page says: "If the package finishes at a loss, you can extend your service for free through our self-extend program." The NHL month adds: "Extensions are not given for days passed unless you are not shown a profit." One day packages get an account credit the next morning instead, and two of them count a small profit as a failure: college basketball pays a $30 credit "If the package does not produce at least $40 in profit across all plays", and NHL "If the package results in a loss (or profit less than $35)". The season packages and the 365 day soccer package carry no guarantee wording at all.

The Doc's Sports terms, which cover every package, say: "Once a product or service has been purchased and delivered or viewed, there are no refunds." They describe a guarantee as "usually the result of incorrect predictions in which case individual accounts will get extended for an additional period of time" and add that "All other services and packages will be reviewed and accounts will be extended at the sole discretion of the staff at Doc's Sports." The terms also say Doc's is "not liable for any losses that are incurred as a result of the information purchased".

So a losing buyer gets more Ferringo picks or store credit, never cash. Losses on the bets themselves are never covered. Because he releases many plays, and his own logs show days with more than 20 football plays, those bet losses can be far larger than the package price.

claims_note: How we checked. Doc's Sports newsletters link "documented" logs for some of his runs. Each log lists every play in a date range the seller picked, with the result, the units and the dollar result at $100 a unit. We copied every row and added them up ourselves. In all three logs our totals matched the totals printed at the top of the log, so the logs are at least internally consistent.

The NHL log runs from 3 Jan 2025 and lists 380 graded plays through 6 May 2026. It shows 184 wins and 196 losses, a 48.4% win rate, for +$9,695. That is $240 less than the "+9,935" on his page. The profit is real on paper but comes from two places: many plays were puck lines and underdogs at plus money, and his 7 unit plays went 23-14 for +$7,060. His 1 unit plays went 73-105 and lost $2,175. Inside this advertised run the total fell by as much as $3,305 from a high point, and December 2025 plus January 2026 lost $1,635 together. By month, the 2025 to 2026 hockey season made about +$3,480 and the January to June 2025 stretch about +$6,215.

The "+6,070" football week is linked to a log covering 11 to 15 Sep 2026. Its football section shows 22-13 for +$3,730 and its daily props section 6-1 for +$1,750, together +$5,480, which is $590 short of the headline. The log includes days with 27 football plays. The 21 to 27 Oct 2026 week matched its claim exactly: 37 plays, 22-15, +$2,880, with 22 plays on a single day. His four plays of 5 units or more that week all won, while his 1 unit plays went 7-7.

Other numbers do not hold together across copies of his own page. The bankroll paragraph, first written around 2014, still says "now" in 2026 and promises over $100,000 from $10,000 in under four years, while his own 2014 article said the same bettor would have "nearly $57,000". In August 2025 the header said "11 OF 16 WINNING FB YRS"; today it says "11 OF 17", so by the seller's own count the 2025 football season was not a winning one. The same check on hockey is consistent: "11 OF 16" in March 2026 became "12 OF 17", which fits the winning 2025 to 2026 hockey season in the log. College basketball is not consistent: the bio said "13 of 17" in August 2025 and March 2026 and says "15 of 20" now, while the header says "14 OF 20". The season special page still gives his top rated college basketball record as 599-398 where his page says 588-392, and puts last season's closing run at +7,910 where his page says +6,780.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that covers his full history. We found no full, time stamped log of every Ferringo pick held by a third party, no outside monitor record and no contest results run by an outside organizer. Our searches found no court or regulator action involving him.

What the seller publishes: runs, subsets and counts of winning seasons on his page, plus a few linked logs for date ranges Doc's chose. The logs show the pick, the result, the units and the dollar result, but no odds column for most picks, no post time and no proof of when each pick was released. The Doc's FAQ says it grades with "the line that is the general consensus at the time of posting", which may not be the line a buyer actually gets.

What the logs we recounted show: a volume service. One football day had 22 plays and another 27. Most plays are 1 or 2 units, and the result swings on a handful of 6 to 8 unit plays. A buyer who bets everything at a flat stake would see a very different record from the unit weighted totals on the page, and the hockey log shows that the small plays lost money over 16 months while the big ones carried the run.
His own 2014 article calls him "a volume handicapper" who "won't hesitate to release 26 plays on a college hoops Saturday". That matches what the logs show in 2026.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Robert Ferringo is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform beyond the recount of Doc's own logs above.
our_data.context: For scale: his page highlights records near 60%, such as 588-392 on college basketball plays rated 5.0 and up, while his own NHL log won 48.4% of its plays. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent buyer evidence about Robert Ferringo is thin and mostly old. One Sportsbook Review thread from 2014 is the only real argument about his results. The rest are passing remarks and reposts of his plays. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found only a handful of independent posts that say anything about Ferringo, on Sportsbook Review (2011 and 2014), TheRX (2025 and 2026) and Sitejabber (2013). The one real discussion, a February 2014 Sportsbook Review thread, is split. A buyer who lost on a top rated basketball total doubted his claimed results given about 30 plays a day, and another member said fading Doc's plays had paid. A different member said they had made a profit three straight years on the college basketball plays even at worse lines, though others in the thread accused them of being Ferringo. The complaint that repeats, in 2011, 2014 and 2026, is volume: people say he sends so many plays that nobody can bet or track them all. Nobody posted a full log either way. In 2026 TheRX members repost his plays in daily threads without grading them, and one reacted with surprise that an MLB total was rated 8 units. We found no Reddit discussion, no BBB file and no news coverage about him. That is too little to call a pattern, so the most useful evidence on this page is Doc's own logs, recounted above.

A Sportsbook Review member opened a thread after losing a large bet on a Ferringo top rated over in basketball. They wrote that he sends about 30 plays a day, that nobody really bets or tracks all of them, and that his claimed results could not be true. They posted no log. Much of the thread is abuse rather than evidence.

In the same thread a member said they had made a profit three straight years with his college basketball plays, that every game had been recorded on a forum the year before, and that the group often did not get his lines and still came out ahead. Another member said they had won 24 units with him on a Saturday. Other members accused the first poster of being Ferringo; we could not check that either way.

Two other members in the thread said Doc's Sports big plays in general tend to lose, and one said fading Doc's plays in college basketball and the NBA had made them around 17 units. Neither posted a record, and neither singled out Ferringo's picks.

In a Sportsbook Review thread about another pick site, a member said they were skeptical of handicappers like Ferringo who put out about 50 units of plays a day and, in their view, bet none of them. It is an opinion with no record attached.

A TheRX service play thread reposted a Ferringo 8 unit play on an MLB over. Another member quoted it and asked whether that really was an 8 star play, which reads as surprise at the rating. TheRX threads like this pass paid plays around for free and do not grade them. The same thread's rules list Doc's Sports among services members should not post.

In a TheRX thread about Doc's Sports, a member who said they track the Doc's handicappers each day wrote that the sellers highlight hot runs and never mention cold streaks, and named the house handicapper and Raphael Esparza as the worst. They did not name Ferringo and did not post a log. We did not verify their figures.
The same TheRX thread was opened by a bettor who said they had used Doc's Sports off and on for more than 10 years and asked for feedback. Nobody in the thread discussed Ferringo's picks.

A Sitejabber reviewer said they had used Ferringo and another Doc's handicapper and recommended the other one, who they said hit about 70 percent over 30 days. They praised timely releases and customer service but said the cost was high. They said nothing about how Ferringo's picks did.
Sitejabber showed Doc's Sports at 1.8 out of 5 from 12 reviews. These reviews are about the whole service, not Ferringo in particular.

Doc's weekly newsletter promotes him with lines such as "came through yet again" and "nearly doubled his clients' bankrolls". These are written by the seller, and two of the three logs it links come out lower than the headline figures when recounted.

Our searches of Reddit, Covers and the open web found no other thread with a real discussion of Ferringo's picks, and no Trustpilot, BBB or news page about him as an individual. Evidence is too thin to say what a typical buyer experiences.

conflicts: Ferringo sells only through Doc's Sports, so the Doc's conflicts apply. The Doc's FAQ says: "We have a list of offshore sports book that we have complete confidence in." On 20 Nov 2026 the free pick on the Doc's homepage still listed the line as "Offered at: BookMaker", and on 7 Nov 2026 that link redirected through a revenue share tracking address to a BookMaker promotion page. Revenue share deals usually pay the referrer a cut of what referred customers lose.
Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live before you follow that advice.

Doc's both sells his picks and grades them, and it chooses which date ranges get a linked log. His free weekly NFL columns and free picks also promote the same store, which offers a "Free $60 Account" to start.
strengths: A named handicapper with a long public writing history at Doc's, including weekly NFL articles through November 2026.
Prices and guarantee terms are written out per package on his page, so a buyer sees the rules before paying.
Doc's links some play by play logs with units and dollar results. They are selective, but they let a buyer recount a claim, and one week we checked matched exactly.
He states his approach openly: many plays, unit ratings from 1 to 8, and a long term view, so buyers know what kind of service to expect.
The linked NHL log shows a profitable 16 month stretch on paper, at plus money prices, even though fewer than half the plays won.
concerns: No full public record. Every headline number is a run, a subset or a season count chosen by the seller, and the linked logs cover date ranges the seller picked.
Two of the three logs we recounted come out lower than the advertised totals (+5,480 against +6,070, and +9,695 against +9,935).
Several advertised figures conflict with each other or with his own 2014 article, including the bankroll promise and the winning season counts.
Very high volume. Logs show 22 and 27 football plays in a day, and the small plays lost money in the hockey log, so a flat stake bettor would see different results.
The guarantee replaces a losing package with more picks or credit. It never returns money, season packages have no guarantee, and betting losses are never covered.
The Doc's FAQ points readers to offshore sportsbooks, and the site carries a sportsbook revenue share link.
checklist: Ask for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
If the seller links a "documented" log, add it up yourself and compare the total with the headline. We found gaps of $240 and $590.
Count units, not wins. A 48% record can show a profit at plus money, and a 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose.
Decide before you buy whether you will bet every play. With 20 or more plays on a busy day, skipping some changes your result.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. At Doc's a losing package earns more picks, never cash.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He is a real handicapper and longtime Doc's Sports writer who sells picks through a store with published prices and a named operator. We could not verify that his picks win over time. Doc's publishes only selected runs and a few linked logs, and two of the three logs we recounted came out lower than the advertised totals.
How much does Robert Ferringo cost?

On 20 Nov 2026 his Doc's page sold one day packages for $25 to $30, weekly packages for $89 to $99, monthly packages for $279 to $325, and longer packages from $495 (rest of the football season) to $850 (NBA season).
Does Robert Ferringo have a verified record?

No. His page shows runs and winning season counts graded by Doc's Sports, and we found no full pick log, outside monitor or contest record. The logs Doc's links are for date ranges it chose. Watchdog has no graded record for him.
What did the Doc's logs show when you recounted them?

The 21 to 27 Oct 2026 football week matched its +2,880 claim. The week sold as +6,070 added up to +5,480 including props. The NHL run sold as +9,935 added up to +9,695 from 184 wins and 196 losses, with the profit coming from plus money prices and a few 7 unit plays.

No cash refunds. Doc's terms say there are no refunds once a product is delivered or viewed. Losing weekly and monthly packages can be extended for free, some one day packages get a $30 credit, and season packages carry no guarantee.

You get a high volume of picks with unit ratings in up to six sports. What is unproven is whether those picks, at the lines a buyer can get and bet the way a buyer bets them, beat the roughly 52.4% needed at -110 over hundreds of plays. If you try him, buy a day or a week and log everything.
